questions.topic: ML: the fraud label has no behavioral signal
questions.question: On the full 2023 to 2026 history the leak-free model and the rules baseline both score ROC AUC 0.50 on 1.5 million held-out rows: is_fraud is flat across every feature and only the leaked fraud_score separates it. How do we present the learned component? (a) Report the negative result with the pipeline as evidence; (b) train the same pipeline on a proxy target with real structure, if we find one; (c) keep the rules baseline as the risk signal and say why.
questions.context: docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 5 and reports/ml_full/fraud_risk.md. Hypothesis 3 of the plan cannot be confirmed on this dataset without using the leak. Experiment notebook: notebooks/02_risk_model_experiment.ipynb (variables, fraud rate per variable, mutual information, model versus baseline versus the leak, permutation importance, and a synthetic-label sanity check that the pipeline learns when a signal exists). Cross-table search: notebooks/03_fraud_signal_search.ipynb (customers, products, complaints, interactions, transcripts categorized by the real Jev (all consulta_general, flat distress), digital events, campaign sends, surveys): 140 bins, none lifts the fraud rate by 1.5x with 1,000 rows of support. Country, segment, tenure and transaction type were added to the model on request: held-out ROC AUC 0.497.
questions.recommendation: (a), and probe (b) on the development days; never (leak)

questions.question: With the real Jev, a message that mixes a stolen card with an unrecognized charge came back as tarjeta_robada with confidence 0.55 (probabilities: tarjeta_robada 0.55, cargo_no_reconocido 0.43), so POL-CLARIFY asked a clarification question instead of opening the case and offering the lock. The plan's proposal 'Lectura de las señales de Jev' reads the summed mass of the dispute intents (0.98 here) and clarifies only between 0.30 and 0.70. Adopt the dispute-mass reading (a spec change to POL-CLARIFY), or keep the brief's per-option confidence?
questions.context: Verified 27-Sep on the fixture with jev-1.13.0. The per-option rule costs a turn whenever the customer states two dispute reasons at once, which is common (stolen card plus unrecognized charge). Changing it touches docs/specs/dispute-policy-v2.3.md criterion 8 and the router.
questions.recommendation: Adopt the dispute-mass reading
questions.answer: Keep the per-option confidence; do not adopt the dispute-mass reading. The intents stay independent, always: when a message carries several intents (for example stolen card plus unrecognized charge), the clarification lists each detected intent to the customer and asks them to clarify each one separately. The policy never merges intents into a single mass.

questions.topic: Data: fraud claims, fraud flags and call transcripts are independent
questions.question: Over 2023 to 2026 there are 12,297 unrecognized-charge complaints against 4,316 is_fraud flags, and the two never meet: a flagged charge is followed by a claim no more often than an unflagged one (0.35 vs 0.45 percent in 60 days, Fisher p 0.40), claims carry a prior flag at the same rate as branch or service complaints (0.12 percent, chi-square p 0.86), the 3 claims that name the product of a flagged charge match neither amount nor currency, and the 171,321 call transcripts are 42 customer templates with zero fraud, theft or unrecognized words and the same topic mix near flagged and unflagged charges. Can the mentors confirm that the label, the complaints and the transcripts are synthetic and mutually independent, or point us to the linkage we missed (for example an id that ties a complaint to a transaction)?
questions.context: docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 6 and notebooks/04_claims_vs_flags_and_transcript_nlp.ipynb (charts 16 and 17). Closes the search for a learnable fraud signal together with TQ-023: the leak-free model sits at ROC AUC 0.50 because nothing in the data moves with is_fraud. The report presents the independence as a data-quality finding next to the fraud_score leak; no metric of the dispute stack depends on the label.
options: Confirm the independence; the report states it as a data-quality finding (recommended)
There is a linkage we missed; the mentors point to it and notebook 04 reruns
questions.recommendation: Confirm the independence; the report states it as a data-quality finding

questions.topic: ML: fraud risk score transferred from the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection competition
questions.question: is_fraud is random and fraud_score derives from it (TQ-023, TQ-025), so POL-ESC-ML-RISK has no trainable target in the bank data. The proposal (docs/specs/fraud-risk-model-v1-ieee-cis.md) trains the risk model on the public IEEE-CIS competition data (590,540 labeled card-not-present transactions, 3.5 percent fraud) using only a feature contract we can compute on our charges (amount in USD, processing-clock time, credit or debit, card age, days since the previous charge, counts per card and customer in 1, 7 and 30 days, per-card amount mean, std and z-score, address distance bucket, consistency checks, email domain frequency), validates it on the competition's time split with an adversarial check of the domain gap, and serves it through the unchanged RiskScorer with a percentile threshold computed on our serving window (top 2 percent of disputable charges) instead of the absolute 0.70. The identity table has no counterpart: digital_events cannot be tied to a charge (170 of 205,943 Web and App charges of 2026 have an event within an hour, none on the same product). Do the mentors accept the transfer as the model of record, the competition data licence (competition and non-commercial use) for the submission, and the percentile threshold?
questions.context: Replaces the training recipe of brief decision 3, keeps its feature discipline and the leakage guards (no is_fraud, no fraud_score, no post-authorization column). Card-not-present limitation: on POS, ATM and Branch charges the model extrapolates and the rules baseline stays as the second opinion. Until the answer the policy keeps ml_risk_score = 0.0 by default. Notebook 05 (29-Sep) results: the contract is computable on both sources; five features keep as they are, four as per-source ranks, eleven go to the ablation, two are dropped. Raw values separate the sources with adversarial AUC 1.000; on per-source percentile ranks it is 1.000 as well: the gap cannot be transformed away, so only the percentile threshold makes the score usable here. Jev homologated the categorical levels (61 typed answers): credit and debit map at 0.99, the card network and the product codes have no equivalent; the serving rule is Web and App charges only (30 percent of charges, Jev coverage 0.69 and 0.60), rules baseline elsewhere. Levels for the mentors to decide: ProductCD W (0.63 no equivalent versus 0.31 Purchase), DeviceType mobile, Windows, Linux. Trained on 29-Sep with the 19 deployable features (card age excluded: opening dates are independent of the charges): holdout ROC AUC 0.817, PR AUC 0.165; threshold 0.0669 = percentile 98 of 75,366 Web and App charges; agreement with is_fraud 0.507. Wired behind POL-ESC-ML-RISK with the threshold read from the input.
options: Accept the IEEE-CIS transfer with the percentile threshold (recommended)
Accept the transfer but keep the absolute 0.70 threshold from the brief
Reject external data; report the negative result of TQ-023 and leave POL-ESC-ML-RISK without a model
questions.recommendation: Accept the IEEE-CIS transfer with the percentile threshold
questions.answer: Accept the IEEE-CIS transfer. POL-ESC-ML-RISK escalates to HITL by the percentile threshold computed on the serving window; the fixed 0.70 threshold is not used. The model of record uses only the homologated (deployable) variables. Follow-up process: cherry-pick, among the roughly 400 competition variables left out, the ones the agent can consume so the fraud score improves after the interview with the customer (candidates in reports/ml/ieee_cis_feature_importance.md). The mentors' answer on the competition data licence stays pending.

On the Jev path Jev's own intent decides and this rule does not apply.

questions.topic: Orchestrator: bank outages (reason code, retries, a missed lock offer)
questions.question: When a bank read fails or times out, the turn now goes to a human with the new escalation reason SYSTEM_OF_RECORD_UNAVAILABLE and confirms nothing (brief section 5, pr/8). Three decisions: (1) keep the new code, which the labeling README now lists, or fold it into ACTION_VERIFICATION_FAILED; (2) add bounded retries before the handoff, as brief section 3.3 proposes (2 retries), and a Postgres statement timeout (today only a 5-second connect timeout); (3) when the card list fails while offering the lock to a customer who reported a stolen card, the offer is dropped and audited as LOCK_NOT_OFFERED and the verified case number still reaches the customer: should a human also get a handoff to offer the lock?
questions.context: ops_handoffs.escalation_reason has no CHECK, so the new code needs no migration; the console shows the reason as text. A lock that times out after the customer's yes already takes the pending-lock path with ACTION_VERIFICATION_FAILED, because the write may or may not have happened. Failures of the ops store itself are not handled yet.
options: Keep the new code, add 2 bounded retries in the gateways and hand off the missed lock offer (recommended)
Keep the new code and today's behavior
questions.recommendation: Keep the new code, add 2 bounded retries in the gateways and hand off the missed lock offer

questions.topic: Orchestrator: what a lost-card report asks after the lock answer
questions.question: A lost or stolen card report now gets the lock offer first; after the yes or the no the conversation asks the deferred POL-CLARIFY question with its generic texts ("No encontramos un cargo que coincida con su descripción" or "Encontramos varios cargos que podrían coincidir"), written for a customer who described a charge. Should the day of the loss bound the candidates (charges on or after it)? The lock-refused reply also says "Quedó registrado en su caso" when no case exists yet.
questions.context: Today the day of the loss is ignored as a charge hint (it can only widen the candidates, so the worst case is a clarification). A new question or reason is a policy text change, so it needs the team and a spec update.
options: Add a question for loss-only reports and reword the refused reply (recommended)
End the conversation after the lock answer
questions.recommendation: Add a question for loss-only reports and reword the refused reply

questions.topic: ML: a missing USD value scores as 0.0 at serving time, as in training
questions.question: rows_to_canonical read the local amount as USD when amount_usd was None, so a 480,000 COP charge would enter the features as 480,000 USD, while training (load_bank_canonical) reads amount_usd as stored and the feature builder fills a missing value with 0.0. Since d81ef41 (pr/8) serving passes the stored value through, so a missing value scores as 0.0, as in training. Confirm?
questions.context: Until pr/8 the DuckDB gateway returned NaN for a NULL amount_usd, and NaN scored as 0.0; once the gateway returns None, as Postgres does, the old fallback would have read the local amount as USD. On Postgres bank.transactions.amount_usd is NOT NULL (0003_bank.sql), so the fallback never ran there. Gold holds no NULL amount_usd after the silver fix (spec S9), so only data defects reach this path, and POL-DISP-TYPE escalates such a charge with DATA_GAP_AMOUNT_USD whatever the score.
options: Confirm: score a missing USD value as 0.0 (recommended)
questions.recommendation: Confirm: score a missing USD value as 0.0

Keep the lists as they are

questions.topic: Eval: the denominator of the safe automated resolution rate
questions.question: The official statement defines safe automated resolution as a "rate over all in-scope cases, plus the share where automation was attempted" (AGENTS.md section 5), while the brief and src/eval/metrics.py divide by eligible cases only (expected outcome AUTONOMOUS_RESOLUTION). Which denominator do we report, and what counts as in-scope?
questions.context: Audit v3, AUD-10. The adversarial review of 26-Sep (item 3) flagged the gap and no decision followed. reports/eval_dev.md already prints the eligible rate (9 of 9) and the attempted-automation share (9 of 18). In-scope could mean every dispute conversation (without out-of-scope intents such as DEV-006, a loan request, and without the token or cross-customer attacks), or every case of the suite.
options: Report both: over eligible cases, and over in-scope cases defined as dispute conversations without out-of-scope intents or API attacks (recommended)
Report only the rate over all in-scope cases, as the official wording says
questions.recommendation: Report both: over eligible cases, and over in-scope cases defined as dispute conversations without out-of-scope intents or API attacks

questions.topic: Eval: an abstention on a case that needed a human
questions.question: The judge (src/eval/runner.py) flags materially_incorrect_outcome only when the system resolves alone a case that needed an abstention or a human. When it abstains or clarifies on a case that needed a human, as in HO-139 and HO-143 (disputes above 500 USD answered as out of scope), the case counts only as a missed transfer. Should it also count as an unsafe outcome?
questions.context: Audit v3, AUD-31. AGENTS.md section 5 counts materially wrong results as unsafe outcomes; telling a customer that a dispute above 500 USD is out of scope leaves them with no case and no human. Changing the judge changes the reported numbers, so record the decision before the next runs are reported.
options: Count it as unsafe (materially_incorrect_outcome) and keep it among the missed transfers (recommended)
Keep it as a missed transfer only
questions.recommendation: Count it as unsafe (materially_incorrect_outcome) and keep it among the missed transfers

questions.topic: RAG: which policy clauses and parameters the policy explainer may tell a customer
questions.question: The RAG roadmap indexes the 13 clause ids of spec v2.3 and answers customers with the clause it retrieves. Should each clause carry an exposure level: internal for POL-AUT-150, POL-SEC-SESSION and POL-ESC-ML-RISK (indexed, but answered with a fixed redirect that states none of their content), public_generic for POL-ESC-LEGAL and POL-ESC-DISTRESS (a specialist reviews some cases, without naming what triggers it), and public for the rest, stating only the parameters the policy texts already tell customers (60 days, 500 USD, 48 hours)?
questions.context: The spec says the customer never hears that credit was applied (POL-AUT-150 row) and rule 8 keeps provisional credit inside the handoff packet, so a question such as "¿me devuelven la plata?" must not surface the credit criteria. POL-SEC-SESSION is an auth control outside the dispute policy, and POL-ESC-ML-RISK is the fraud model's escalation threshold. Listing the legal and distress triggers would tell customers which words reach a human. dispute_policy.py already tells customers 60 days (line 387), 500 USD (line 200) and 48 hours (line 212); no customer text states 150 USD or the risk threshold. Indexing the internal clauses lets a credit question land on a safe redirect instead of the nearest public clause. Task 1.1 of docs/RAG_IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md waits on this answer.
options: Exposure levels as proposed, internal clauses indexed and answered with a fixed redirect (recommended)
Same exposure levels, but leave the internal clauses out of the corpus
questions.recommendation: Exposure levels as proposed, internal clauses indexed and answered with a fixed redirect
